title: [SEP2-3] A DM's or self-group's "CO" can be a single-user identity host, which gives the relay the
description: Review finding SEP2-3: A DM's or self-group's "CO" can be a single-user identity host, which gives the relay the initiator's identity; no billing-DID rule covers identity hosts (lens SEP2). Location: spec/10-relays.md:777, :696; spec/12-security.md:53; spec/02-identity.md:496; ARCHITECTURE.md:395-396 (§9); spec/10-relays.md:545. Fix: As suggested. 10:696 restricts the billing DID only from records "that identif[y] a Space", so nothing stops a self-hosting individual from using their own DID. agora-q6-billing-did makes anonymity depend on the CO serving many Spaces, and §9 accepts "A CO with one Space gets none", but no counterpart exists for identity hosts. agora-did-methods allows the individually chosen hosts that create this case. Extend 10:696 with "and, for an identity host, MUST NOT be a DID of a user it serves or appear in any DID document, Pkarr record or other user-identifying record". Add the §9 bullet ("DM and self-group anonymity at the IO is only as large as the initiator's identity host; a host serving one user gives none"). Qualify 12:53 ("does not learn who is in a DM, except as above") and 10:545. Full text: notes/review2/SEP2-verified.md and notes/review2/SEP2.md.
